_about: The UNIRA living standard (Constitution Article 10c), essential and comfortable levels. Every value carries its source or is marked ASSUMPTION. The constitutional definition is not changed to improve results.

food.unit: kcal eaten per person per day
food.source: essential: Millward-Hopkins et al. 2020 DLE (2,000-2,150); comfortable: UNIRA comfortable diet (v65 thresholds, planetary-health composition)

water.unit: % of people with at least basic drinking water (essential) / safely managed (comfortable)
water.source: UN SDG 6.1 service ladders (WHO/UNICEF JMP), via World Bank SH.H2O.BASW.ZS / SH.H2O.SMDW.ZS

sanitation.unit: % of people with at least basic sanitation

electricity.unit: % of people with access to electricity

clean_cooking.unit: % of people with clean cooking fuels and technologies

energy.unit: GJ of final energy per person per year, all uses (heating/cooling, mobility, goods, services)
energy.source: essential: Millward-Hopkins et al. 2020 decent living energy; comfortable: UNIRA comfortable level within a 1.5 C-class pathway (v66)
energy.climate_adjustment: ASSUMPTION: x (1 + 0.25 x (|latitude of capital| - 25) / 40), clipped to 0.85-1.25, renormalised so the world mean is unchanged

housing.unit: m2 of residential floor area per person
housing.source: essential: Millward-Hopkins et al. 2020 (15 m2); comfortable: UNIRA comfortable level (v66)
housing.household_note: ASSUMPTION: per-person floor area; household composition adjusts allocations in practice (Article 10d.5)

health.unit: doctors, nurses and midwives per 10,000 people, weighted by age and disease burden (rule 37)
health.source: essential: WHO 2016 SDG health-workforce threshold; comfortable: EU level (v65); weighting v79/health_need

education.unit: % gross secondary enrolment; primary pupils per teacher
education.source: enrolment: SDG 4 (universal secondary completion); 40 pupils per teacher: UNESCO upper benchmark commonly used; 20: ASSUMPTION near OECD averages

internet.source: ASSUMPTION thresholds (universal meaningful connectivity is the goal); data ITU via World Bank IT.NET.USER.ZS

goods_and_discretionary.unit: share of France's 2022 household goods consumption per person (clothing, furniture, equipment, leisure goods, personal choices)
goods_and_discretionary.source: ASSUMPTION: UNIRA favours repair, reuse and durability (Article 11); delivered by needs-based quotas (Article 10d) from world goods capacity (v85)

mobility.note: essential and comfortable mobility (Millward-Hopkins 2020: 5,000-15,000 passenger-km per person per year) is included in the energy level and in the labour estimate; no country data on passenger-km were available

scenarios._notes: energy build 0.67/1.2/1.8 TW-equivalent (v67); health training plans (v66); housing build growth (v70); access_speed selects the median (1.0), top quarter (1.5) or top tenth (2.5) of the yearly coverage gains actually achieved by lagging countries since 2010 (measured); each country uses at least its own measured pace; teacher stock growth in deficit regions (ASSUMPTION); automation_by_year_30 = share of each sector's automation potential reached by year 30 (ASSUMPTION)

labour._about: Hours per person per year France 2022 embodied in household and government final consumption (v63/io), mapped to basket domains and scaled to the UNIRA standard. Scaling factors are ASSUMPTIONS unless stated.

scale_to_unira.energy: computed: 40 GJ / France final energy per person
scale_to_unira._why: ASSUMPTIONS: less waste and meat (food); more public transport (mobility); repair and reuse (goods); no advertising, speculation or competitive duplication (trade, finance, business: v63 avoidable output); leaner administration

automation_potential._source: ASSUMPTION informed by task-based automation studies (high for routine physical and data tasks, low for care and teaching); human-only floor as in v86
